Visioner BREAKING | 🇺🇦 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Ukraine has reportedly struck a Russian oil infrastructure facility deep inside Bashkortostan, targeting a site operated by Transneft-Ural. Preliminary reports indicate that the attack targeted the Subkhankulovo oil pumping station in the Tuymazinsky District of Russia’s Republic of Bashkortostan. The facility is part of the country’s oil transportation infrastructure. The extent of the damage and any potential disruption to operations have not yet been established. Oil pumping stations play an important role in transporting crude oil through Russia’s pipeline network. Strikes against such facilities could disrupt energy logistics and increase pressure on infrastructure far from the Ukrainian border. The reported attack also highlights Ukraine’s continued focus on extending the reach of its strikes into Russian territory. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

DPRK leader Kim Jong Un called for tactical nuclear weapons to be used across multiple domains, calling the task "important and urgent," during a tour of nuclear material production sites and the Nuclear Weapons Institute, KCNA reported on Thursday. Kim declared that the country's nuclear status is enshrined in its constitution, that its nuclear capability is now "a reality," and that denying it amounts to a recognition of failure. He warned that the United States is encouraging its allies in Northeast Asia to acquire nuclear-powered submarines through the AUKUS precedent, and to build a nuclear alliance system based on nuclear sharing. The tour was Kim's fourth reported visit to a nuclear facility since September 2024, and it came days after Pyongyang snubbed overtures from US President Donald Trump for talks.
